requirements.text: XML Services shall be segmented.
The XS shall have the ability to redefine or reset names of connect descriptors to database server instances.
At a minimum, the session time-out values shall be user definable and be able to be reset prior to initialization of a user session.
The data management services shall support managing various types of data, database architectures and platforms that includes hardware and software at the specified sites.
The Registry shall provide standard APIs as specified in Appendix B .
The XS function shall provide standard APIs as specified in Appendix C .
The XS shall internally interface (transparent to the operator) with the existing data elements of the DBIF, DAC, and COTS RDBMS products.
The Registry software shall be portable and required to execute on COE-compliant platforms.
The XS software shall be delivered in accordance with DII COE guidelines.

Manager services shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) and maintain an immutable audit log of all administrative actions, including user creation, privilege escalation, and configuration changes.
Maintenance operations involving user privileges shall require multi-factor authentication or dual-authorization (two-person rule) and must be logged in accordance with DII COE security standards.
Define the specific failure domains and isolation boundaries for the segmented XML Services to ensure that a failure in one segment does not propagate to others.
Specify the target operating systems, hardware architectures, and required compatibility standards (e.g., POSIX compliance levels) to ensure verifiable portability.
Define specific performance targets (e.g., 'The system shall maintain a response time of <X>ms for <Y> concurrent requests under a load of <Z> transactions per second').
Define a specific Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) for the mirrored database services.

OPEN: The document mentions 'Discretionary Access Control (DAC)' in the glossary but does not define the security requirements for enforcing these controls within the XML Services. - The XS shall enforce Discretionary Access Control (DAC) on all XML Registry objects, ensuring that access permissions are validated against the subject's identity before any read, write, or modification operation.

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'degraded communications environments' but provides no quantitative reliability targets (e.g., MTBF, recovery time objectives, or retry policies) for these conditions. - Define the maximum allowable downtime or recovery time objective (RTO) for XML services when operating in a degraded communications environment.

OPEN: The requirement to interface with COTS RDBMS products lacks error handling or failure mode specifications for when those external dependencies are unreachable. - Define the expected failure handling behavior (e.g., circuit breaking, graceful degradation, or queuing) when the interface to DBIF, DAC, or COTS RDBMS products fails.

OPEN: The PRD mentions a goal of dynamically changing session time values based on network performance but provides no latency or throughput requirements for the network management or DBMS monitoring capabilities. - Specify the maximum latency allowed for the monitoring system to detect network degradation and trigger a session time-out adjustment.

OPEN: The PRD does not define the expected scale of the XML Registry (e.g., number of tags, concurrent users, or volume of metadata) that the system must support. - Define the capacity requirements for the Registry, such as: 'The Registry shall support a minimum of <X> concurrent users and <Y> registered XML tags while maintaining a search response time of <Z> seconds.'
